userStories.title: Incremental Graph Diff — Replace Full Re-Import
acceptanceCriteria: IncrementalGraphDiffService.diffAndApply() computes a diff and applies only the delta.
Stored graph is loaded from GraphNode + GraphLink Prisma tables (§5 above); not from LanceDB.
When newNodes has 100 nodes and stored has 90, added=10 and removed=0.
When a stored node is absent from newNodes, it is deleted from both GraphNode table and LanceDB (by graphify nodeId / RAG sourceId).
When a node exists in both with unchanged content, it is skipped (no re-index).
diffAndApply is called by the existing importGraphify endpoint (replaces the current deleteAllBySourceType logic).
DiffResult.indexed reflects only the number of nodes actually written to LanceDB (not the total).
A diff-and-apply of 500 unchanged nodes + 10 added + 5 removed completes in under 2 seconds.
DiffResult includes durationMs for performance monitoring.
Only actors with role admin, developer, or agent can call importGraphify (enforced at controller layer).
suggestedCriteria: importGraphify response migration preserves compatibility for existing domain-writer consumers during transition (either updated consumers or alias fields imported/cleared).
When newNodes is empty and stored graph has nodes, all stored nodes are removed from GraphNode and LanceDB.
When vector-store upsert/delete fails after durable graph writes, the operation surfaces a retryable failure and does not silently report success.

userStories.title: AST/Symbol Index Pipeline
acceptanceCriteria: AstIndexService.indexCommit() parses source files and stores symbol metadata in the Symbol Prisma table (§5).
Symbol.symbolId uses the convention {repoId}:{filePath}::{SymbolName} and is globally unique within a project.
getCallers(symbolId) returns all symbols that include this symbol in their JSON callers list.
getCallees(symbolId) returns all symbols in this symbol's JSON callees list.
When indexCommit is called with files=[{path: 'src/auth.ts', content: '...'}], only src/auth.ts is parsed (incremental — existing symbols for unchanged files are preserved).
Symbol.signature captures parameter types and return type (e.g. (userId: string): Promise<User>).
Indexing is triggered by a code_commit outbox event (fired by the VCS webhook handler — see US-004).
A commit with 20 files (avg 200 lines each) is indexed in under 30 seconds.
Only actors with role admin or developer can call AstIndexService.indexCommit() directly (not agents); role checked at controller layer.
Parser failures for one file are recorded in the result and do not prevent other files in the same commit from being indexed.
The code_commit handler resolves changed file contents before calling indexCommit(); the webhook controller only enqueues commit metadata.
suggestedCriteria: Before inserting symbols for a changed file, prior Symbol rows for that (projectId, repoId, file) are replaced to avoid stale symbol accumulation.
indexCommit with empty files returns symbolsIndexed=0 and filesIndexed=0 without error.
Symbol ID collision suffixing is deterministic across re-indexes of the same file and commit content.

userStories.title: Ticket/Entity Graph Builder
acceptanceCriteria: EntityGraphService.rebuildGraph(projectId) rebuilds all entity nodes and links for a project.
Entity graph data is persisted in EntityNode and EntityLink tables, not only in Phase 2's in-memory EntityStore.
onTicketEvent(status_changed) updates the entity node for that ticket (if it exists).
onGraphifyImport() extracts service entities from graphify nodes with type=code_module.

The initial implementation does not require a Ticket.serviceId column; service linkage works from current Koda fields (gitRefFile, labels, linked code/module references) until an explicit service relation exists.
getRelatedEntities(projectId, entityId, depth=2) returns all entities reachable within 2 hops.
getIncidentImpact(projectId, incidentTicketId) returns all entities linked to the incident.
Service entities extracted from graphify inherit tags from the graphify node (e.g. ['backend', 'auth']).
Entity graph is updated incrementally via outbox fan-out (no full rebuild on every event).
A graph with 500 nodes and 2000 edges returns getRelatedEntities in under 50ms.
suggestedCriteria: Entity linkage heuristics apply deterministic precedence when multiple rules match the same ticket-service relationship.
getIncidentImpact returns empty affected arrays when an incident has no linked entities.
rebuildGraph removes stale EntityLink rows that no longer have valid source/target entities.

userStories.title: VCS Webhook Handler → code_commit Outbox Event
userStories.description:
Goal — Extend the existing project-scoped VCS webhook surface so push/code-intel events enqueue code_commit outbox records instead of doing code indexing synchronously.

Motivation — Push webhooks usually contain file names, not full source contents, so the outbox handler must resolve file contents before calling the AST indexer and the controller must stay thin.

Approach — The webhook controller stays on POST /projects/:slug/vcs-webhook, validates the provider signature with the existing x-hub-signature-256 flow, verifies the payload has a repository identifier, ref, commits[], and sender identifier, and enqueues one code_commit outbox event per commit with { repoId, commitHash, ref, changedFiles }. The code_commit outbox handler resolves changed file contents before calling AstIndexService.indexCommit(). Replaying the same commitHash within a 5-minute window must not create duplicate outbox rows.

Interface — VcsWebhookController continues to own the public webhook route, and the outbox payload for code indexing is { repoId, commitHash, ref, changedFiles }.
acceptanceCriteria: VcsWebhookController extends the existing project-scoped webhook surface at POST /projects/:slug/vcs-webhook to handle push/code-intel events.
Webhook payload is validated: presence of repository identifier, ref, commits[], and sender identifier (sender.id, sender.login, or provider equivalent).
For each commit in the push, a code_commit outbox event is enqueued with { repoId, commitHash, ref, changedFiles }.
AstIndexService.indexCommit() is called by the code_commit outbox handler, not synchronously by the webhook controller.
If event enqueueing fails, the webhook logs the failure and returns a non-2xx response so the provider can retry.
GitHub webhook signature verification reuses the existing x-hub-signature-256 flow, and invalid signatures return 401.
The webhook secret continues to come from the project's VCS connection record and is never hard-coded.
Pushing the same commitHash twice does not create duplicate outbox events within a 5-minute window.
suggestedCriteria: Push routing is explicitly handled in VcsWebhookService (eventType='push') and no longer falls through as unknown.
changedFiles is built as the union of added/modified/removed entries from each commit payload.
When file content resolution encounters binary or oversized files, the handler skips those files and records warnings while indexing remaining files.

userStories.title: getChangeImpact API
acceptanceCriteria: GET /projects/:slug/codeintel/impact?repoId=X&commitHash=Y&changedFiles=file1,file2 returns a ChangeImpactResult.
impactedSymbols contains symbols whose file matches any entry in changedFiles.
impactedServices contains service entities linked to impacted symbols through matching Symbol.file to GraphNode.sourceFile or EntityNode.sourceId.
impactedTickets contains tickets linked to any impactedServices.
impactScore is a number from 0 to 100 computed by the formula in the design section.
When called with a ticketId, the result includes provenance source metadata pointing to that ticket.
The endpoint returns in under 5 seconds for a commit touching up to 50 files.
Only actors with role admin, developer, or agent can call this endpoint, and the role check happens at the controller layer.
suggestedCriteria: impactScore returns 0 when no symbols, services, tickets, or incidents are linked to changedFiles.
linkedIncidents is computed deterministically from incident-type entities reachable from impacted services/tickets.
When a changedFiles entry matches no symbols, impactedSymbols is empty and the endpoint still returns 200 with a valid score.

userStories.title: CanonicalStateService Snapshot Read Layer
acceptanceCriteria: CanonicalStateService.getSnapshot(query) returns retrievedAt set to the server timestamp.
When ticketIds are provided, tickets contains only tickets in the requested projectId.
When timeWindow is provided, recentEvents contains only events in the window and is ordered by createdAt DESC.
activeDecisions is populated from active MemoryItem rows with kind='DECISION'.
A non-existent or unauthorized projectId throws the same KodaError or Nathapp exception style used by earlier memory endpoints.
The service performs canonical Prisma reads only and does not query LanceDB, BM25, the entity graph, or other derived stores.
suggestedCriteria: When ticketIds is an empty array, tickets returns as an empty array.
When timeWindow.from is set, recentEvents only includes events with createdAt >= from.
activeDecisions excludes non-active decision records (e.g., superseded/rejected equivalents).

analysis:
Phase 4 will be delivered as an incremental, project-isolated foundation that replaces destructive graph re-import with durable diffing, adds deterministic AST/symbol indexing, introduces a durable ticket/entity graph, and exposes change-impact + canonical snapshot read APIs. This synthesis keeps Proposal 2’s codebase-aware migration path, Proposal 1’s clear architecture/SLOs, and Proposal 3’s concrete schema direction, while explicitly resolving blocking ambiguities from the critiques.

Resolved decisions:
1. Dependency direction: IncrementalGraphDiffService is a standalone graph service (depends on graph persistence + vector-store abstractions), and RagService delegates to it; no RagService↔diff-service cycle.
2. Story dependency cycle removed: US-002 depends on US-001; US-004 depends on US-001 and US-002.
3. Access control semantics: endpoint role checks use project membership roles (ADMIN/DEVELOPER/AGENT where specified) at controller layer, not a global role expansion.
4. Compatibility break is explicitly scoped: importGraphify return-shape migration must update KodaDomainWriter/tests (or provide backward-compatible aliases during transition).
5. Durable store is source of truth; LanceDB is derived index. Partial-failure handling is treated as retryable/index-reconciliation behavior.
6. SQLite compatibility is enforced via JSON-encoded string fields with repository/service validation.

Implementation order:
- US-001 incremental graph diff
- US-002 AST/symbol indexing pipeline
- US-003 durable entity graph builder
- US-004 webhook→outbox code_commit path
- US-005 getChangeImpact API
- US-006 CanonicalStateService read layer

This sequence preserves existing Phase 2 retrieval and Phase 3 semantic-memory responsibilities, keeps graphify imports project-scoped and gated by Project.graphifyEnabled, and minimizes regression risk by introducing durable persistence and async ingestion first, then composition APIs.
